title: The Crowned King: -ott/-ett/-t Participles as Titles

sections.content: Historical Hungarian is full of fixed royal epithets built exactly this way: 'a megkoronázott király' ('the crowned king'), 'a felkent uralkodó' ('the anointed ruler'). These aren't just descriptions — they're the standard way Hungarian refers to a monarch's status after a specific ceremony, and you'll need them constantly when talking about István's coronation.

items.spanish: István Kr.u. 1000 körül, karácsonykor lett megkoronázott király.
items.english: István became a crowned king around the year 1000, at Christmas.

items.spanish: A felkent uralkodó ettől kezdve Isten kegyelméből uralkodott, nem csak a törzsi hagyomány alapján.
items.english: From then on, the anointed ruler ruled by the grace of God, not merely by tribal tradition.

items.spanish: A pápa által elismert királyság erősebb helyzetben volt, mint egy egyszerű törzsi fejedelemség.
items.english: A kingdom recognized by the pope was in a stronger position than a simple tribal principality.

sections.content: Notice how much these forms compress: 'a megkoronázott király' packs an entire historical fact into one word. When you can say 'a megkoronázott király' instead of the longer 'a király, akit megkoronáztak' ('the king who was crowned'), your Hungarian sounds noticeably more natural — and more like how Hungarians actually talk about their own history.
